extracted_claims.text: Article 43 of the AI Act gives high-risk AI providers two conformity-assessment routes: internal control under Annex VI, or a quality-management-system plus technical-documentation assessment performed by a notified body under Annex VII.

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU sectoral legislation listed in Section A of Annex I (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements.
A new conformity assessment is required if a high-risk AI system is substantially modified, except for predetermined changes in systems that continue to learn after being placed on the market.

Article 46 allows a market surveillance authority, by derogation from Article 43 and upon justified request, to authorise placing a specific high-risk AI system on the market for a limited period for exceptional public-security, health, environmental or infrastructure-protection reasons.

Under Article 43, a provider may choose any notified body for the Annex VII procedure, except where the system is to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or EU institutions/bodies, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body.

Annex VII (point 4.5) requires that, where necessary and after other verification means are exhausted, a notified body be granted access to training and trained models of the AI system, subject to existing EU intellectual-property and confidentiality law.
Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes the administrative framework for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies under the AI Act.

Articles 44 and 45 of the AI Act address certificates issued by notified bodies and the information obligations of notified bodies, respectively, within the Standards/Conformity Assessment section (Articles 40-51).

Under the 2021/2022 Commission proposal text of Article 43, the notified-body (Annex VII-type) route applied specifically to high-risk systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometrics) when harmonised standards or common specifications had been applied; otherwise an internal-control procedure could be used.

Commentary on the adopted Article 43 states that the Annex VII/notified-body route is required for high-risk AI systems referred to in points 2 to 8 of Annex III under certain conditions, a broader scope than the original proposal's 'point 1' language.

Commentary interprets Annex VII as mandatory for biometric identification systems and 'certain critical infrastructure AI', with most other high-risk systems eligible for the Annex VI self-assessment route.

High-risk AI obligations under the EU AI Act are described as applying in full from August 2026 (with some sources citing August 2, 2026 as a key compliance deadline for declarations of conformity and SaaS providers).
GPAI (general-purpose AI model) obligations under the AI Act applied from August 2025.

A Commission proposal (COM(2025)836, document ST-15708-2025-INIT) would add a new Annex XIV listing codes/categories for AI systems in the Commission's NANDO notified-body database and would amend Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements for aviation; this is a legislative proposal, not yet confirmed as adopted law by the sources.
As of March 2026, the notified-body ecosystem specifically for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing across Member States and capacity described as limited.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act in the context of medical device AI (MDR/IVDR interplay).

Sources project that notified bodies designated specifically under the AI Act will begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments only after 2026, interacting with existing MDR/IVDR notified-body assessments.
As of October 2025, the NANDO database listed 51 MDR-designated and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies (medical devices under Regulation (EU) 2017/745/746), not AI Act-specific designations.

Under the separate Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), notified-body rules began applying on 11 June 2026, with a target of 11 December 2026 for sufficient notified-body capacity and full application from 11 December 2027; as of late June 2026, zero notified bodies had been designated under the CRA.

The Commission may adopt delegated acts under Article 43(5) to update Annex VI ('CA Procedure based on Internal Control') and Annex VII ('Conformity Based on Assessment of Quality Management System and Assessment of Technical Documentation') in light of technical progress, without needing to revise the AI Act itself.

contradictions.claim_a: The 2021/2022 proposal version of Article 43 limited the notified-body (Annex VII) conformity assessment route specifically to high-risk systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometrics).
contradictions.claim_b: Current official guidance on the adopted Article 43 describes a separate rule for high-risk AI systems referred to in points 2 to 8 of Annex III, indicating the final adopted provision has a broader or differently structured scope than the original proposal.
contradictions.description: Sources 14 and 19 reflect the 2021-2022 Commission proposal text limiting the notified-body route to 'point 1 of Annex III', while sources 1, 11, 12, 13 (official EU guidance, undated but reflecting the adopted Regulation 2024/1689) reference distinct treatment for 'points 2 to 8 of Annex III', suggesting the proposal and final adopted law differ in scope and structure; sources do not clarify exactly how the final Article 43 reconciles these points.

contradictions.claim_a: As of March 2026, the AI Act notified-body designation process was described as still ongoing/being built, implying no or very few designations existed yet.
contradictions.claim_b: As of April 2026, a separate source states no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act (in the medical-device AI context).
contradictions.description: Both sources agree no AI Act notified bodies were designated by Q1-Q2 2026, but they are dated differently (March 2026 vs April 2026) and come from different outlets describing the same unresolved status, raising the question of whether any partial progress occurred between these dates that neither source documents.

open_issues: No source identifies any specific notified body that has actually been designated under the AI Act (as opposed to under MDR/IVDR or other regimes) as of the research date (October 2026).

It is unclear from the sources whether the Commission proposal (COM(2025)836) adding Annex XIV/NANDO integration and amending Regulation 2018/1139 has been formally adopted, or remains pending in the legislative process.
The sources do not clarify how conformity assessments already performed by existing MDR/IVDR notified bodies will be reconciled or converted into AI Act-specific designations.

The precise current (post-proposal) text of Article 43 covering Annex III points 2-8 and its relationship to Annex VII is not fully quoted in the sources, leaving the exact scope of mandatory notified-body involvement unclear.
No source gives a definitive count or list of notified bodies specifically designated for AI Act conformity assessment as distinct from CRA, MDR, or IVDR notified bodies.

It is unclear whether the August 2026 'full application' deadline for high-risk obligations creates a compliance gap given the near-total absence of designated AI Act notified bodies reported through early-to-mid 2026.
report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
Available sources describe, at low confidence, a two-route conformity assessment structure under Article 43 of the EU AI Act — internal control (Annex VI) or third-party assessment by a notified body (Annex VII) ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)). More firmly established, at high confidence, is that systems covered by existing EU sectoral legislation must follow sectoral assessment procedures with added AI-specific verification ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Separately, evidence suggests the notified-body ecosystem specific to the AI Act remains largely undeveloped as of early-to-mid 2026, creating uncertainty about practical enforcement capacity ahead of the August 2026 compliance deadline (low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
At low confidence, commentary describes Article 43 as offering high-risk AI providers two routes: internal control under Annex VI, or a combined quality-management-system and technical-documentation assessment conducted by a notified body under Annex VII ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)). At medium confidence, commentary on the adopted text indicates the Annex VII/notified-body route applies to systems referred to in points 2 to 8 of Annex III under certain conditions ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)), a broader scope than the original 2021 Commission proposal, which had limited the notified-body route to point 1 of Annex III (biometrics) where harmonised standards applied (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf), [Artificial-Intelligence-Act.com](https://www.artificial-intelligence-act.com/Artificial_Intelligence_Act_Article_43_(Proposal_25.11.2022).html)). Some commentary further interprets Annex VII as mandatory mainly for biometric identification and certain critical-infrastructure systems, with most other high-risk systems eligible for self-assessment (low confidence) ([Quantamix](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)).

At high confidence, for high-risk systems already covered by sectoral EU legislation (e.g., medical devices, machinery) listed in Annex I Section A, providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

### Modification, Derogation, and Notified-Body Powers
At medium confidence, a new conformity assessment is required for substantial modifications to a high-risk system, except for predetermined changes in continuously-learning systems ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to authorise temporary market placement of a system, by derogation from Article 43, for exceptional public-security, health, environmental or infrastructure reasons (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Providers may generally select any notified body, except where systems are used by law enforcement, immigration, asylum, or EU institutions, in which case the market surveillance authority performs the notified-body function (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Annex VII (point 4.5) allows notified bodies access to training and trained models when necessary, subject to IP and confidentiality law (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)). Articles 44 and 45 govern certificates and notified bodies' information obligations (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-60)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
No source identifies a specific notified body formally designated under the AI Act. As of March 2026, the AI Act-specific notified-body ecosystem was still being built, with designation processes ongoing and capacity limited (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)). As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been designated in the MDR/IVDR-AI interplay context (low confidence) ([AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)). By contrast, as of October 2025 the NANDO database listed 51 MDR- and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies — these are sectoral, not AI Act-specific designations (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). A Commission proposal (COM(2025)836) would add a new Annex XIV for NANDO coding and amend aviation regulation 2018/1139, but adoption status is unclear (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
The 2021-2022 proposal text (point 1 of Annex III only) contradicts later guidance referencing points 2-8, and sources do not clarify the exact reconciliation (low confidence, flagged). Two sources (March vs. April 2026) independently report no designated AI Act notified bodies, but neither documents interim progress. The core "two-route" claim (claim_001, 0.17) and the "mandatory-for-biometrics-only" interpretation (claim_011, 0.14) are both below the 0.4 threshold and should be treated as provisional rather than settled law.

## Knowledge Gaps
No specific AI Act-designated notified body has been identified; the relationship between MDR/IVDR assessments and AI Act requirements is unresolved; the final scope of Article 43/Annex III points 2-8 is not fully quoted; and whether a compliance gap exists given the August 2026 deadline remains unanswered.

# Conformity Assessment Procedures for High-Risk AI Systems Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes two main conformity assessment routes for high-risk AI systems — internal control (Annex VI) and third-party assessment by a notified body (Annex VII) — with the applicable route depending on the Annex III category and whether the system falls under existing EU sectoral legislation (medium-to-high confidence). However, evidence suggests the notified-body ecosystem specific to the AI Act remains largely undeveloped as of early-to-mid 2026, creating uncertainty about practical enforcement capacity ahead of the August 2026 compliance deadline (low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Routes
Article 43 of the AI Act offers high-risk AI providers two routes: internal control under Annex VI, or a combined quality-management-system and technical-documentation assessment conducted by a notified body under Annex VII (low confidence) ([PowerQuant](https://powerquant.eu/en/ai-act-conformity-assessment), [FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)). Commentary on the adopted text indicates the Annex VII/notified-body route applies to systems referred to in points 2 to 8 of Annex III under certain conditions (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)), a broader scope than the original 2021 Commission proposal, which had limited the notified-body route to point 1 of Annex III (biometrics) where harmonised standards applied (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf), [Artificial-Intelligence-Act.com](https://www.artificial-intelligence-act.com/Artificial_Intelligence_Act_Article_43_(Proposal_25.11.2022).html)). Some commentary further interprets Annex VII as mandatory mainly for biometric identification and certain critical-infrastructure systems, with most other high-risk systems eligible for self-assessment (low confidence) ([Quantamix](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)).

For high-risk systems already covered by sectoral EU legislation (e.g., medical devices, machinery) listed in Annex I Section A, providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedure, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43), [VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai)).

### Modification, Derogation, and Notified-Body Powers
A new conformity assessment is required for substantial modifications to a high-risk system, except for predetermined changes in continuously-learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to authorise temporary market placement of a system, by derogation from Article 43, for exceptional public-security, health, environmental or infrastructure reasons (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)). Providers may generally select any notified body, except where systems are used by law enforcement, immigration, asylum, or EU institutions, in which case the market surveillance authority performs the notified-body function (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/ga/ai-act/article-43)). Annex VII (point 4.5) allows notified bodies access to training and trained models when necessary, subject to IP and confidentiality law (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)). Articles 44 and 45 govern certificates and notified bodies' information obligations (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-60)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
No source identifies a specific notified body formally designated under the AI Act. As of March 2026, the AI Act-specific notified-body ecosystem was still being built, with designation processes ongoing and capacity limited (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)). As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been designated in the MDR/IVDR-AI interplay context (low confidence) ([AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)). By contrast, as of October 2025 the NANDO database listed 51 MDR- and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies — these are sectoral, not AI Act-specific designations (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). A Commission proposal (COM(2025)836) would add a new Annex XIV for NANDO coding and amend aviation regulation 2018/1139, but adoption status is unclear (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
The 2021-2022 proposal text (point 1 of Annex III only) contradicts later guidance referencing points 2-8, and sources do not clarify the exact reconciliation (low confidence, flagged). Two sources (March vs. April 2026) independently report no designated AI Act notified bodies, but neither documents interim progress. Multiple low-confidence claims (0.03–0.20) regarding delegated acts, proposal status, and timelines warrant caution.

## Knowledge Gaps
No specific AI Act-designated notified body has been identified; the relationship between MDR/IVDR assessments and AI Act requirements is unresolved; the final scope of Article 43/Annex III points 2-8 is not fully quoted; and whether a compliance gap exists given the August 2026 deadline remains unanswered.
